pillar_reactions.evidence: Rep delivered kettlebells and mobility as one system — 'every part of physical health is encompassed into one thing, into one system' — and the prospect answered 'Yes... that sounds, that sounds right' and later 'totally makes sense'. He had already primed himself positively earlier: 'I honestly feel it's a really good workout. So I think that's where I should be.'

The only question he asked in the whole presentation was about the eating protocol: 'Is the philosophy behind the diet like more of a fasting kind of thing? Or is it like eat throughout the day?' Rep clarified two to three larger meals with fasting, and the prospect closed it out with 'Yeah, absolutely.'

24/7 access to Trevor and the weekly check-in were presented in full — 'we want to hold you accountable to the guy with no love handles, arm definition, no pain' — and the prospect responded only with 'Yes. Cool.' No questions, no visible engagement. Earlier he had signalled the underlying need himself: 'I never had anybody there watching me telling me, okay, this is right, this is wrong.'

anchors.raw: There was a guy that was an influencer there for a while. His name was Greg Plitt. I went on his, uh, site and it taught me a lot that I needed to know about, uh, um, lifting and what to live. And what muscles to work and how and all that kind of thing.
anchors.note: Two years of results were obtained from a low-cost online resource, and the prospect states plainly 'I've never had a trainer.' He has no history of paying for coaching at all, so $6,000 is his first-ever coaching purchase and has nothing to be measured against. The rep never surfaced or reframed this, which left the price sitting on an empty anchor.

anchors.raw: I'm selling my house right now. I have three interested parties. So, with the proceeds from that, I can do it.
anchors.note: A large, near-term liquidity event means the price was never contested on value — only on timing. The rep had a strong position to hold $6,000 and wait, and chose to discount the entry point instead.

unmet_demand.want: Bulkier arms — 'not definition, just bulkier, because... no matter how much I lift, it feels like not much happens on my biceps'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep's own positioning of the training outcome directly contradicts it: 'What you get from kettlebells is more like a fighter physique... more like a boxer, UFC fighter kind of physique, rather than a bodybuilder.' Kettlebell full-body work does not prioritise isolated bicep hypertrophy, and the prospect's stated arm goal was never revisited or reconciled after he named it.

unmet_demand.want: Resolution of four chronic joint complaints — problematic left knee, tight left hip and lower back, tight neck with reduced rotation, intermittent shoulder — at age 55
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The rep promised the mobility programming would target them ('we want to have the focus areas on the places of pain') on the strength of a visual movement assessment only. Whether coached mobility work resolves multi-site chronic pain in a 55-year-old, with no clinical assessment and no clinician involved, is not established on this call.
